notes: Primary ask: contractually-backed Dedicated pool for clinical LLM workloads (PHI-sensitive) - must support HIPAA controls and VPC-only ingress/egress.

Throughput negotiation summary: customer requests a minimum sustained throughput of 25,000 tokens/sec for the dedicated pool during business hours (08:00-20:00 PT), with a concurrency cap to protect latency.
Concurrency proposal: Nightingale prefers a soft cap of 256 concurrent streams per tenant with token-based fair-share; Redwood proposed 192 guaranteed concurrency with overflow queueing.

Burst policy: customer wants 40% burst above sustained for up to 10 minutes per hour for traffic spikes. Redwood countered with tiered burst (+30% for 10m, +20% for 30m/day) tied to reserved buffer capacity.

Latency SLOs: target p95 inference latency <300ms for 32-token completions (chat routing) and p99 <700ms. Redwood suggests p95 <250ms for top-tier models on dedicated SKUs; still debating p99 SLA credit thresholds.
Penalty & credits: Nightingale requested service credits for breach (0.5% ARR per 1 hour below SLO beyond threshold). Redwood proposed capped credits and remediation windows; legal to reconcile.
Reserved GPU planning: initial commit request = 8x H100-equivalent GPUs (multi-model pool); rollback/scale clauses: 6-month minimum term with quarterly scaling ops.
Model routing & fallbacks: requirement to pin clinical-tuned model versions; automatic fallback to quantized variant acceptable but must preserve hallucination safeguards and audit logs.
Data residency: all inference and logs must stay in US-East region for now; discuss hybrid on-prem batch for older records.
Cost sensitivity: high. Nightingale wants guaranteed per-token pricing tiers under the committed capacity; asks for Optimize recommendations to hit cost targets.
Open technical risks: end-to-end latency spikes when KV cache miss rate >35%; need pre-warming guidance and warmup windows in contract.
